dedupe_keys.name: meta and wri high resolution 1 m global canopy height maps

description: These maps give tree canopy height at 1 m resolution for the whole land surface, predicted from very high resolution satellite imagery by a self-supervised vision transformer trained with aerial lidar. It covers the globe for an analysed period of 2009 to 2020, with about eighty per cent of the imagery acquired between 2018 and 2020, and reports a mean absolute error of about 2.8 m. It was produced by Meta together with the World Resources Institute, described by Tolan and co-authors in Remote Sensing of Environment (2024), with source imagery from Maxar. The data are available as an Earth Engine image collection curated in the awesome-gee community catalogue, with an Earth Engine viewer app, under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence and free of charge; the model is also released on GitHub. Caveats: heights are model predictions from one imagery date per place, and the catalogue entry was last updated in 2024. It is useful for mapping urban trees and green infrastructure, vegetation clearance around power lines and roads, and shade and heat analysis in climate adaptation studies; a related record is the CLMS high resolution tree cover and forests layer.
